title: Futur simple
description: Say what will happen with one-word future forms.

guide.summary: The futur simple is the one-word future: je parlerai, nous irons. Learn the six endings, then the handful of verbs whose stem is not simply the infinitive.

sections.title: The endings: one set for every verb
sections.text: A future form is a stem plus an ending, in one word. The endings never change, whatever the verb. For -er and -ir verbs the stem is the whole infinitive, with nothing removed.
steps: Take the infinitive as it is: parler, finir, sortir.
Find the subject and go to its row.
Add that ending straight onto the infinitive.

examples.en: Tomorrow I will finish this book.

watch: The endings are the present of avoir: ai, as, a, ons, ez, ont. An r always comes just before them.
-ai (je) and -as (tu) differ by one letter, and so do -ons (nous) and -ont (ils). Check the subject before the last letters.
je parlerai is the future; je parlerais, with a final s, is the conditional (I would speak).

sections.title: -re verbs: drop the final e
sections.text: An infinitive ending in -re loses that e before the ending. The r stays: it is the mark of the future.
steps: Write the infinitive and check whether it ends in -re.
Cross out that final e, and keep the r.
Add the ending for the subject.

examples.fr: Elle lira un livre dans le train.
examples.en: She will read a book on the train.

examples.fr: Nous attendrons le bus devant l’école.
examples.en: We will wait for the bus in front of the school.

watch: Never keep the e: prendreai, lirera and attenderons do not exist.
Build on the infinitive, not on the present stem: lire gives lir-, not lis-.

sections.title: Être, avoir, aller, faire
sections.text: The four most used verbs have stems that look nothing like their infinitives. The endings are still the same six.
steps: Name the verb first: être, avoir, aller or faire.
Take its stem from the table; never build on the infinitive.
Add the ending for the subject.

examples.fr: Quand tu viendras, nous irons au cinéma.
examples.en: When you come, we will go to the cinema.
In May I will be twenty.

watch: Age, hunger and the weather use avoir or faire, not être: j’aurai vingt ans, il fera froid.
Forms built on the infinitive (avera, allera, fairera, êtrera) do not exist.

sections.title: The other irregular stems
sections.text: A short list of very common verbs. The stem always ends in r, and the endings do not change.
steps: Ask whether the verb is on this list before you touch the infinitive.
Take its stem from the table, then add the ending for the subject.
Falloir and pleuvoir exist only with il.

examples.en: We will have to leave early tomorrow.

watch: Pourr-, verr- and enverr- have two r: one from the stem, one from the future.
Do not confuse il pleuvra (it will rain) with il pleura, from pleurer, to cry.

sections.title: -er verbs that change their spelling
sections.text: A few -er verbs change the stem in the future. Unlike in the present, the change is there in every person.
steps: Say the je form of the present: j’achète, j’appelle, je paie.
Carry that change into the stem, for every person.
Add the ending for the subject.

examples.en: I will buy a new bag.
I will call you tomorrow morning.

watch: Acheter and lever take a grave accent (è); appeler and jeter double the consonant. Do not swap the two.
The change is in every person: nous achèterons, not nous acheterons.
With payer both spellings are accepted, and only the y may change: never drop the e of the stem.
Verbs like préférer and espérer keep their é in the future: je préférerai.

sections.title: After quand, French uses the future
sections.text: English says “when I arrive, I will call you”, with a present after when. French puts both verbs in the future when both events are still to come.

rows: when I arrive, I will call you
when he comes, we will eat
when we have money, we will buy
quand nous aurons de l’argent, nous achèterons

steps: Find the verb that follows quand.
Ask whether its event is still to come; if it is, put it in the future.
Put the other verb in the future too, unless it is an order: quand tu arriveras, appelle-moi.

examples.fr: Quand tu viendras, nous irons au cinéma.
examples.en: When you come, we will go to the cinema.
When she gets home, she will eat.

watch: Quand je finis mes études describes a habit; for a single future event the verb moves to the future.
Lorsque and dès que work the same way: dès que tu arriveras, appelle-moi.

sections.title: Words that call for the future
sections.text: A time marker tells you which tense to use: markers that point forward take the future, markers that point back take a past tense.
steps: Find the time marker and decide which way it points.
If it points forward, put the verb in the future; if it points back, use a past tense.
Then match the ending to the subject.

examples.fr: Dans dix ans, nous aurons une grande maison.
examples.en: In ten years we will have a big house.

examples.fr: L’année prochaine, nous visiterons le Canada.
examples.en: Next year we will visit Canada.

watch: Dans dix ans means in ten years’ time; il y a dix ans means ten years ago.
For a close or spoken plan the futur proche is natural (je vais partir). The one-word future suits more distant or more formal plans, and it is the tense used after quand.

steps: Take the infinitive whole: nothing is removed.
Find the subject and its ending: -ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont.
Read the last letters back and check they match the subject.
Start from the infinitive, not from the present form.
If it ends in -re, drop the e and keep the r.
Add the ending for the subject.
Name the verb: être, avoir, aller or faire.
Use its special future stem instead of the infinitive.
Add the ending for the subject.
Check whether the verb is one of the irregular ones (venir, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, savoir, voir, envoyer, falloir, pleuvoir).
Use its stem from the table, never the infinitive.
Add the ending, and count the r: some stems carry two.
Say the je form of the present: j’achète, j’appelle, je paie.
Carry that change into the stem and keep it in every person.
Add the ending for the subject.
Find the verb after quand.
Ask whether its event is still to come.
If it is, put it in the future, whatever English does.
Check the other verb of the sentence as well.
Find the time marker and decide whether it points forward or back.
If it points forward, use the future.
Match the ending to the subject.

exercises.hint: Keep the whole infinitive and add the nous ending.
exercises.feedback: The futur simple starts from the full infinitive, then adds the ending for the person.
exercises.explanation: Parler + -ons gives nous parlerons.

mistakes.why: -ez is the ending for vous. The subject given here is nous, which has an ending of its own.
-ont belongs to ils and elles, several people. The subject given is nous.
That is the present tense, we speak. A future form keeps the whole infinitive, so an r stands before the ending.
That is the conditional, we would speak. The future ending for nous has no i in it.

exercises.hint: Start from finir and add the ils ending.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending: the ils form of the future ends in -ont.
exercises.explanation: Finir + -ont gives ils finiront.

mistakes.why: -ons is the nous ending. The subject given here is ils.
-a is the singular il/elle ending. Ils stands for several people.
That is the present tense, they finish. A future form keeps the whole infinitive, with r before the ending.
That is the conditional, they would finish. The future ending is shorter and has no i.

exercises.instruction: Write choisir in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Keep the full infinitive and add the tu ending.
exercises.feedback: The tu ending of the future is -as, added to the whole infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Choisir + -as gives tu choisiras.

mistakes.why: -a is the il/elle ending. The subject in the sentence is tu, which takes a different one.
-ez goes with vous. The subject here is tu, one person you know well.
That is the present tense, you choose. The sentence is about tonight, still to come.
That is the conditional, you would choose, not a future form.

exercises.hint: All four are future forms. Which ending goes with vous?
exercises.feedback: Match the ending to the subject vous.
exercises.explanation: Vous takes the ending -ez: vous inviterez.

mistakes.why: -ons is the nous ending, for a group including you. The subject is vous.
-ont is the ils/elles ending, for people talked about. The subject is vous, the people spoken to.
-ai is the je ending, for one speaker. The subject is vous.

exercises.source: Nous mangerez à la maison demain.
answers: Nous mangerons à la maison demain.
exercises.hint: Look at the ending of the verb and at the subject.
exercises.feedback: The verb ending does not match nous.
exercises.explanation: With nous, the future ending is -ons: nous mangerons.

answers: Nous mangerez à la maison demain.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: -ez belongs to vous, while the subject here is nous.

answers: Nous mangeront à la maison demain.
mistakes.why: -ont belongs to ils and elles, so the ending still does not match the subject.

answers: Nous mangeons à la maison demain.
mistakes.why: That is the present tense. Demain points forward, so the verb needs the r of the infinitive before its ending.

answers: Nous mangions à la maison demain.
mistakes.why: That is the imparfait, we used to eat, a past tense; demain points forward.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence in the futur simple.

exercises.hint: Two tiles are future forms of parler. Only one matches je.
exercises.feedback: Check which future ending belongs with je.
exercises.explanation: Je takes the ending -ai: je parlerai. Parleras is the tu form.

answers: Je parleras à ma sœur ce soir.
mistakes.why: Parleras is the tu form. The subject tile here is Je, so the last letters must change.

answers: Je parlerai ma sœur ce soir.

exercises.hint: Start from the infinitive of the verb and add the il ending.
exercises.feedback: The future is built on the full infinitive travailler.
exercises.explanation: Travailler + -a gives il travaillera.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged, in the present tense.

exercises.hint: Verbs ending in -re lose one letter before the ending.
exercises.feedback: Remove the final e of prendre before adding the ending.
exercises.explanation: Prendre loses its e: prendr- + -ai gives je prendrai.

mistakes.why: The final e of the infinitive has been kept. An -re verb loses it before the ending.

exercises.instruction: Write attendre in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: Drop the final e of the infinitive, then add the nous ending.
exercises.feedback: An -re verb keeps its r but not its final e in the future.
exercises.explanation: Attendre becomes attendr-, and nous adds -ons: nous attendrons.

mistakes.why: The e of attendre has been kept before the ending; an -re verb drops it.
-ont is the ils/elles ending. The subject in the sentence is nous.
That is the present tense, we are waiting. A future form keeps the r of the stem.
That is the conditional, we would wait, not the future.

exercises.source: Elle ____ un livre dans le train.
exercises.hint: The verb is lire. What happens to its final e?
exercises.feedback: The future of an -re verb starts from the infinitive without its e.
exercises.explanation: Lire becomes lir-, and elle adds -a: elle lira.

mistakes.why: That keeps the e of the infinitive and adds a second r. Once the e is gone, only the ending is added.
Lis- is the present stem, as in nous lisons. The future is built on the infinitive instead.
That invents a stem by repeating part of the infinitive. Nothing is added between the stem and the ending.

exercises.hint: Look at the stem of the verb: one letter is too many.
exercises.feedback: An -re verb drops its final e before the future ending.
exercises.explanation: Prendre becomes prendr-, so the ils form is ils prendront.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the e of the infinitive is still sitting before the ending.
The e has only moved. An -re verb keeps no e at all before the ending.
-ons is the nous ending, but the subject of this sentence is ils.
That is the present tense, they take. Demain asks for a future form.

exercises.instruction: Put the sentence in the futur simple.
exercises.hint: The infinitive is vendre. Remove its last letter, then add the tu ending.
exercises.feedback: Build the future on vendr-, not on the present form.
exercises.explanation: Vendre becomes vendr-, and tu adds -as: tu vendras.

mistakes.why: The e of the infinitive has been kept; an -re verb drops it before the ending.
-a is the il/elle ending. The subject here is tu.
That is the sentence unchanged, in the present tense.
That is the conditional, you would sell, not the future.

exercises.explanation: The future stem of faire is fer-, and ils adds -ont: ils feront.
